title: Diagnostic accuracy study
note: Four things decide whether the reported accuracy is real: who was tested, what the test was judged against, whether the two results were read independently, and whether everyone made it through to the end. Prevalence then decides what a positive result is worth. An undescribed method is Unclear, not a failure.

items.question: Were the participants taken consecutively, or at random, from the mix of people in whom this test would really be used?
items.why: A test separates obvious cases from healthy volunteers far more cleanly than it separates the difficult middle, so a hand-picked sample flatters both sensitivity and specificity.
lookFor: where participants came from, and at what point in the diagnostic pathway
definite cases set against healthy volunteers, recruited as two separate groups
exclusions of atypical, severe or difficult patients
whether recruitment was consecutive or left to convenience

items.question: Was the comparison the test was judged against strong enough to stand as the truth for this condition, and was the same one used for everyone?
items.why: Every mistake in that comparison is charged to the test under study, so a weak standard can make an accurate test look wrong, or a poor test look better than it is.
lookFor: what served as the truth: histology, culture, imaging, an adjudication panel, or follow-up
its own known error rate, and whether the authors acknowledge it
different standards used for different participants
clinical follow-up used as the standard for those who tested negative

items.question: Were the two readings kept apart, so that neither the person interpreting the test nor the one applying the standard knew the other result?
items.why: An interpreter who has seen the other result drifts toward agreeing with it, which manufactures accuracy that would never appear in everyday practice.
lookFor: blinding stated in both directions, not just one
what clinical information the reader had while interpreting
how many readers there were, and how far they agreed
the order in which the test and the standard were carried out

items.question: Did everyone go on to the same reference check, including the participants whose test came back negative?
items.why: When only the positives are confirmed, the test's own misses are never counted, and sensitivity is calculated from a group already trimmed of them.
lookFor: how many in each result group were checked against the standard
a weaker or different standard used for the negatives
participants who left before the standard could be applied
a flow diagram that accounts for everyone who was tested

items.question: Was the cut-off dividing a positive from a negative result fixed before the data were examined, rather than chosen to suit this sample?
items.why: A threshold tuned on the same patients it is reported from performs worse in the next group, sometimes by a wide margin.
lookFor: the threshold stated in advance, with a source for it
a curve used to pick the best-performing point in these data
several thresholds analysed but only one carried into the conclusion
separate samples used to develop and then to test the cut-off

items.question: Are indeterminate, failed and missing results reported and accounted for, and was the interval between the two tests short enough that the condition could not change?
items.why: Quietly dropping uninterpretable results removes the hardest patients from the denominator, and a long gap lets people recover or deteriorate between the two measurements.
lookFor: the number of failed or uninterpretable tests, given by group
how those results were handled in the analysis, rather than passed over
the time between the test and the reference check
treatment started in between that could alter the condition

items.question: Are sensitivity and specificity reported with confidence intervals, and can the raw counts behind them be recovered?
items.why: Accuracy estimated from a few dozen patients can move by tens of percentage points, and a single figure with no interval hides how unstable it is.
lookFor: the four counts of the two-by-two table, or enough numbers to rebuild them
a confidence interval on each measure
how many participants actually had the condition
likelihood ratios or predictive values reported alongside

items.question: Is it clear how common the condition was among those tested, given that this governs what a positive result actually means?
items.why: Sensitivity and specificity stay roughly steady while predictive values move with prevalence, so a test that shines in a sample full of disease can return mostly false alarms where the condition is rare.
lookFor: the number with the condition over the number tested
predictive values quoted, and the prevalence they assume
a sample deliberately enriched with known cases
the setting participants were recruited from, and its usual case mix

items.question: Would the test be used at the same point in the pathway, on similar patients, and with comparable equipment and operator skill, in your own setting?
items.why: Accuracy depends on who is tested and on who performs and reads the test, and the chance of disease among your patients decides what a positive or a negative result is actually worth to them.
lookFor: the stage of the pathway at which the test was applied
operator experience, equipment, and laboratory or field conditions
how the prevalence in your patients compares with the study sample
what would change for the patient once the result is known

info.title: Funding & conflicts
info.prompt: Who funded the study, what role did the funder or sponsor have in the design, conduct, analysis and reporting, and what relevant conflicts of interest were declared?
info.why: Industry funding is not itself a risk of bias, and a trial paid for by a manufacturer is not wrong for that reason. What matters is what the sponsor was in a position to do, and what was declared, so record these as facts and let the methodological items above carry the judgement.

fields.label: Funder
fields.hint: Who paid: name the company, agency, charity or grant. Record "not stated" when no funding statement is given.

fields.label: Sponsor or funder role
fields.hint: What they did in design, conduct, data collection and custody, analysis, writing, and the decision to publish. A named funder with no role described is "unclear", not "none".

fields.label: Author conflicts declared
fields.hint: Payments, advisory or speaker roles, employment, stock or patents relevant to this intervention, and whether any declaration statement appears at all.

fields.label: Where this came from
fields.hint: Which document told you: the published abstract, the funding statement in the full text, the disclosure forms, or the registry record. Say if you only had one of them.
